bug_semantics: LiquidJS treated a lexically resolved pathname under a configured template root as proof that the file ultimately opened was under that root. Node's file APIs then followed symlinks, so an attacker-controlled symlink located inside a trusted partials/layouts/root directory could target any readable file outside the directory; include, render, or layout would parse and render the external target.
flaw_origin: Commit 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 first introduced filesystem-backed template loading and the include tag. Its index.js handleCache() resolved the requested name with path.resolve(this.options.root, filepath) and immediately passed that non-canonical pathname to fs.readFileSync(), while tags/include.js routed an evaluated include name into handleCache(). That is the first complete path-check/path-construction-to-file-open mechanism that follows an in-root symlink without validating the target; later Loader.withinDir(), FS.contains(), file moves, and separate partials/layouts roots preserved or re-expressed the same flaw rather than introducing it.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 shows author and committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>, timestamp 2016-06-24, subject 'tag:include', and no message body, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Made-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-56p5-8mhr-2fph describes the pathname-versus-realpath mismatch and demonstrates partials/link.liquid pointing outside the trusted root; the assigned advisory bundle records affected liquidjs versions <=10.25.2 and first patched version 10.25.3.

At the vulnerable tip abc058be0f33d6372cd2216f4945183167abeb25, git blame src/fs/fs-impl.ts lines 44-48 attributes contains(root,file)—nodeResolve(root), separator normalization, then file.startsWith(root)—to aebeae9e1bbb8472af7788dfd09a08cb6de58e1c. git log -L traces that function to aebeae9e; the predecessor Loader.withinDir() to 9cfa43b8aee6a980f39d99f1cdb2be730ca21731; and the inline referenced.startsWith(dir) checks through a3455ebd0b207141c34630c0af44d917db2ca1dd and the Loader introduced by b9ae479b653a34fadb98c324c4683dd1fdd31af1. These are later representations of lexical containment, not the first unsafe file open.

git show 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 shows the atomic first mechanism: index.js added renderFile()/handleCache(), path.resolve(this.options.root, filepath), and fs.readFileSync(filepath), and new tags/include.js evaluated the include name and called liquid.handleCache(filepath). The commit's package.json version was 1.1.4; git tag --contains reports v1.2.0 as the first repository tag containing it, followed by every tagged release through the affected v10.25.2 boundary.

Immediate-parent verification was direct: git ls-tree -r 21bde3cb6d1096d7c03f5a047683cb3a83f8b4d2 -- tags/include.js returned no path; git diff --name-status parent..8fbbec089 reported 'A tags/include.js'; and git grep -E 'handleCache|renderFile|readFileSync' 21bde3cb6d1096d7c03f5a047683cb3a83f8b4d2 -- index.js returned no matches. Thus the include/file-loading path and vulnerable open are absent from the immediate parent.

PR #867 (https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/pull/867) landed as 529dd67eeb6b125637623d6a723601f0938d3613. Its src/fs/fs-impl.ts change makes async and sync contains() resolve both root and candidate with realpath/realpathSync before prefix comparison, and its tests create an in-root symlink to an outside file and require contains/containsSync to return false.

The PR squash was cross-checked against its source branch: abc058be0f33d6372cd2216f4945183167abeb25..origin/fix-fs-contains contains cca3da6147fbc59a5a78875015295327a9ee59e9, b181b08543ed69b081c72fc3ba59f6b5159d9fe9, and 3538864119abdc7e2b82705950c9f3235c5c2235; the landed 529dd67 commit contains the complete realpath remediation. This fix-side squash does not change the atomic, non-squash BIC fields.

Version ancestry is exact: v10.25.2 resolves to 521177e3f63c160c2e093cc4f2b151f51f333f45 and does not contain 529dd67eeb6b125637623d6a723601f0938d3613; v10.25.3 resolves to release commit 8f69a0839903d85c7b5c9097e39ecce6ac3eab05 whose parent is 529dd67eeb6b125637623d6a723601f0938d3613. The v10.25.3 first-party release page lists 'use realpath for fs.contains (#867) (529dd67)'.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by checking or constructing only a lexical path and then allowing the filesystem to dereference it. Starting from the advisory and fix, blame and git log -L lead to the 2021 FS.contains() helper, but stopping there would misclassify a refactor as the BIC. Following its predecessor Loader.withinDir() and inline startsWith checks leads to the 2021 Loader, and following the actual resolve-to-read data flow farther back reaches 8fbbec089: the first commit that added include/renderFile filesystem loading, rooted path.resolve(), and an unchecked fs.readFileSync() sink. Its immediate parent contains none of that capability, so 8fbbec089 is the smallest real first-writer. The flaw survived the later partials/layouts split and lexical containment helpers until 529dd67 canonicalized both sides with realpath; the vulnerable and patched tags straddle that fix exactly. Only the 8fbbec089 commit object controls attribution: it is a 2016 human-authored commit with no AI marker. AI markers on the 2026 fix squash are fix-only and therefore irrelevant to BIC attribution. The closed verdict is NOT_AI.
